plain: A higher-ranked instruction lending some of its authority to content that would otherwise have none.
eli5: Mum saying "do what the recipe card says", so the card now counts, but only for cooking.
technical: In the Model Spec, the only way no-authority content (a file, a tool output) gains authority: an applicable instruction delegates to it, and only as far as the delegator could grant; the agentic-privacy report adds that delegated authority should narrow at each hop (trust attenuation).
